findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State concrete default values for child_traversal (per-direct-child step cost) and fixed_overhead in step 2, grounded in the observed 5-10 requests/child cost cited in the Problem section.
evidence: 'budget = per_criterion x c + child_traversal x direct_children (epics/parents) + fixed_overhead'
No numeric value given for child_traversal or fixed_overhead
AC2: 'childful ticket sizes strictly larger than a childless one at equal criteria count' — a strict-inequality-only constraint
findings.finding: Step 2's evidence-surface formula introduces two coefficients — child_traversal (per direct child) and fixed_overhead — but assigns them no numeric values. The acceptance criteria constrain only the CHILDLESS output (6-AC epic >=80 requests, 15-AC epic >=180 — both derivable from per_criterion=24/floor_min=160 with zero child term) and merely require 'childful sizes strictly larger than childless', which any positive coefficient satisfies. The actual child_traversal and fixed_overhead magnitudes are left for the executor to choose.
scenarios: Executor picks an arbitrary child_traversal (e.g. 1) that under-provisions epics traversing many children, re-creating the exhaustion the plan set out to fix
findings.suggested_fix: Pin child_traversal to the observed cost (e.g. steps equivalent to ~10 requests per direct child) and a fixed_overhead for initial show_ticket + description parse, then add an oracle-pin AC for a specific childful count (e.g. an epic with N direct children sizes to >= X requests).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the reuse-safety claim: merge_finalizer_with_bank preserves finalizer met-downgrades (only the evidence_sufficient marker is bank-sourced), so either scope a change to merge_finalizer_with_bank to re-stamp met from the bank for seeded records, or drop the 'a seeded credit cannot be silently lost' guarantee and its RED test as currently worded.
evidence: Plan quote: 'merge_finalizer_with_bank (bank = source of truth post-1788) re-stamps any finalizer downgrade of a seeded record back from the bank — a seeded credit cannot be silently lost to prompt conservatism; RED test: finalizer echo that drops a seeded criterion still yields the credited verdict.'

Code (completion_verdict_assembly.py:158-160): docstring — 'preserving the finalizer's own judgments (including a cross-criterion downgrade of a banked met=true). The bank is the source of truth for the evidence_sufficient marker'
Code (:171-174): an echoed record appends `existing` (the finalizer's record, its own met) via _restamp_marker; only the marker is bank-sourced
Code (_restamp_marker :140-143): sets/pops only 'evidence_sufficient', never 'met'
findings.finding: The plan asserts merge_finalizer_with_bank '(bank = source of truth post-1788) re-stamps any finalizer downgrade of a seeded record back from the bank — a seeded credit cannot be silently lost to prompt conservatism'. This is refuted by the implementation: merge_finalizer_with_bank preserves the finalizer's OWN met judgment on an echoed record and its docstring explicitly states it keeps 'a cross-criterion downgrade of a banked met=true'; the only thing re-stamped from the bank is the evidence_sufficient insufficiency marker (_restamp_marker), NOT the met verdict. A finalizer echo that drops a seeded PASS to met:false therefore stays met:false — exactly the loss the plan claims cannot happen.
findings.location: Plan §3 (credit-vs-evaluate protocol) / AC line 3 (seeding + RED test) — merge_finalizer_with_bank at src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_verdict_assembly.py:147-210, _restamp_marker at :135-144
scenarios: A re-verify seeds a valid cached PASS; the LLM finalizer (prompt-conservative) echoes that criterion as met:false; merge keeps met:false, the ticket fails to close, and the plan's RED test ('finalizer echo that drops a seeded criterion still yields the credited verdict') cannot pass against the current merge.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit edit to merge_finalizer_with_bank (completion_verdict_assembly.py) that, for records seeded from the cross-run PASS cache, restores met=true (not just the marker) from the seeded bank entry regardless of finalizer echo, and scope its own RED test there; then re-anchor the AC #3 RED test to that seam.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the direct-child file_impact BLOB fingerprint is actually computed: `_subtree_impacts` yields whole-subtree path frequencies (excluding the root), not direct-child blob shas — either name a direct-children-only enumeration + blob-sha resolution, or adjust the plan to the data `_subtree_impacts` really returns.
evidence: completion_prefetch.py:257-281 docstring: 'BFS the subtree ... The root's own file_impact is NOT counted here' and returns dict[str,int] frequency
Plan claims direct-child scope but _subtree_impacts is whole-subtree and path-frequency, not blob-sha and not direct-only
_subtree_impacts lives in completion_prefetch.py, not completion_banking.py where BankStamps/resolve_bank_stamps sit
findings.finding: The plan names `_subtree_impacts` as the seam for 'the union of direct-child file_impact blobs', but that function (completion_prefetch.py:257) BFS-walks the ENTIRE subtree (all descendants, not just direct children), returns a {path: count} frequency dict of PATH NAMES (not blob shas / a fingerprint), and explicitly excludes the root's own file_impact. It cannot as-is produce a direct-child blob fingerprint.
findings.location: Plan section 3 (cross-run PASS cache), phrase 'the union of direct-child file_impact blobs (the `_subtree_impacts` seam)'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the mechanism by which seeded/banked criteria are EXCLUDED from the primary (and successor) work surface — e.g. the primary criterion-id manifest omits already-banked ids — so 'spend budget only on unproven criteria' actually holds on the primary run, not just the successor remainder.
evidence: completion_recovery.py:527-544 primary manifest lists all `expected` criteria regardless of bank contents
completion_recovery.py:495 primary.run runs before any recovery/remainder scoping
Plan does not state the primary manifest (or successor remainder) excludes already-banked/seeded criterion ids
findings.finding: The plan credits cached PASS entries by seeding them into the run-scoped CriterionBank at run start so 'the bounded search targets only unproven criteria', but does not specify how the primary/successor is told to SKIP seeded criteria. On a re-verify the primary run launches FIRST (completion_recovery.py:495) carrying a manifest that lists ALL criteria (primary_criteria_manifest, :540), and only on exhaustion does _recover/_run_successors scope to the remainder. A pre-seeded bank entry does not by itself remove a criterion from the primary's work surface.
findings.location: Plan section 3 'seeded into the run's CriterionBank verbatim, so the bounded search targets only unproven criteria'; AC line 'spends budget only on unproven criteria'
scenarios: A re-verify with all criteria seeded still launches a full primary run over every criterion, so budget is NOT confined to unproven criteria and the exhaustion-convergence claim does not hold on the primary path

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how a seeded validated-PASS credit survives a finalizer DOWNGRADE (echoed met:false): either add a met-restamp rule to merge_finalizer_with_bank for still-valid seeded entries and reconcile it with the existing intentional preservation of the finalizer's cross-criterion met=true downgrade (docstring/completion_verdict_assembly.py:158, 171-174), or drop the 'cannot be silently lost' claim and the AC3 RED test that depends on it.
evidence: Plan text: "merge_finalizer_with_bank (bank = source of truth post-1788) re-stamps any finalizer downgrade of a seeded record back from the bank — a seeded credit cannot be silently lost to prompt conservatism; RED test: finalizer echo that drops a seeded criterion still yields the credited verdict."
completion_verdict_assembly.py:135-144 _restamp_marker only sets/pops `evidence_sufficient`; it never restores `met` from the bank entry.
completion_verdict_assembly.py:171-174: for an echoed finalizer record with a bool `met`, the merge keeps `existing` (the finalizer's own met) and only re-stamps the marker.

merge_finalizer_with_bank docstring (line 156-160): it 'preserv[es] the finalizer's own judgments (including a cross-criterion downgrade of a banked met=true)' — i.e. the bank is source of truth for the MARKER, not for `met`.

Post-1788 (ticket 1d71) design comment: 'merge_finalizer_with_bank re-stamps EVERY record from its bank entry via _restamp_marker (stamps a still-unmet echo over a marked entry; strips model-minted markers ...)' — scope is the marker, not met.
findings.finding: AC3 asserts merge_finalizer_with_bank re-stamps a finalizer's DOWNGRADE of a seeded PASS record back from the bank so 'a seeded credit cannot be silently lost to prompt conservatism', but the referenced seam does not do this: _restamp_marker re-stamps only the evidence_sufficient marker, and the merge preserves the finalizer's own met value on echoed records.
findings.location: Plan section 'Plan' item 3 (Credit-vs-evaluate protocol / Finalizer interaction) and Acceptance criterion 3 ('RED test: finalizer echo that drops a seeded criterion still yields the credited verdict')
scenarios: Re-verify seeds a cached PASS into the run bank; the finalizer echoes that criterion but conservatively emits met:false; the merge preserves met:false, so the seeded credit IS lost and the verdict stays FAIL — the opposite of the plan's claim and its pinned RED test.

A finalizer omits the seeded criterion entirely (not echoed): the backfill branch (line 176-185) sets met from the bank entry, so an OMITTED seeded PASS is credited but a DOWNGRADED (echoed met:false) one is not — an asymmetry the plan does not distinguish.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit rule: for a seeded entry that is (a) validated-PASS and (b) whose scoped fingerprint still matches at run start, merge_finalizer_with_bank restores met=true from the bank over a finalizer echo, while a non-seeded same-run banked met=true remains subject to the finalizer's cross-criterion downgrade. Mark the seeded entries (e.g. a `seeded: true`/`credited` flag on the bank record) so _restamp_marker/merge can distinguish 'authoritative prior PASS' from 'this-run provisional', and pin the asymmetry (echoed-downgrade vs omitted) in the RED test.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that an unparseable/invalid cache entry is ignored (treated as a cache miss -> re-verify) rather than aborting the run, and add a RED test for a malformed entry.
evidence: 'still-valid entries are SEEDED into the run's CriterionBank verbatim'
Atomic tmp+rename covers WRITE integrity but not READ-side handling of a malformed/legacy entry
ABSENCE: no 'on parse failure, ignore entry and re-verify' statement
findings.finding: The plan does not state consumer tolerance for a CORRUPT or unreadable cache entry. Reads at run start (CriterionBank.for_run seeding) assume well-formed JSON; a truncated/partial file (e.g. from an interrupted non-atomic writer, external tampering, or format drift) has no described graceful-degradation path.
scenarios: A partially written or schema-drifted cache file causes seeding to throw, failing the whole verify run instead of degrading to re-verification

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define a RETIRE/cleanup path for the completion_verdicts cache (e.g. drop superseded entries for a ticket on write, or TTL/prune sweep) and add a covering acceptance criterion.
evidence: 'written ONLY on a validated PASS record at finalize (atomic tmp+rename ...)'
Invalidation described only as key-miss ('key each entry by ...') — no deletion of superseded entries
ABSENCE: no cleanup/eviction/TTL/retire step in the plan or any acceptance criterion
findings.finding: The new persistent verdict cache at .rebar/cache/completion_verdicts/<ticket>/<hash>.json has no RETIRE/cleanup/eviction path. Entries are written per validated-PASS keyed by (criterion-text hash, scoped fingerprint); when a fingerprint or criterion text changes a NEW key/file is written but the STALE file is never removed, so the cache accumulates unboundedly across the ticket's lifetime and across all closed tickets.
scenarios: A ticket re-verified many times over months leaves one .json per (criterion,fingerprint) combination, most stale and never read
Repo-wide .rebar/cache/completion_verdicts/ grows without bound as tickets close
findings.suggested_fix: On finalize write for a ticket, delete stale entries whose keys no longer match the current criterion set / fingerprint; or add a bounded prune (per-ticket keep-latest-N or age-based sweep). Add an AC asserting stale entries are removed.
